Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the sideswipe collision you
were involved in while driving in Conroe, Texas. Is it all right if I record this conversation?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please state your full name and the best number to reach you.
A: I'd rtaher keep those details off the recording for now, but I can provide them to the adjuster file afterward.
Q: That works. Can you walk me through what happened leading up to the collision?
A: I was changing lanes to move into the right lane because I needed to get off at the next exit. I checked my mirror,
saw nothing rihgt beside me, and signaled. As I started to move over, the other vehicle came up on my right side and
we made contact along the passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see the ohter vehicle before you started to merge?
A: Not clearly. It was in the blind spot area, and I didn't catch it until I was already partially over.
Q: How fast were you each traveling?
A: I'd estimate I was around the speed of traffic, maybe a little under the limit. The other car seemed to be moving a
bit faster than I was.
Q: Did either vehicle leave the roadway or strike anything else?
A: No. Both of us pulled onto the shoulder after the impact. Nothing else was hit.
Q: Did you feel any injuries at the scene?
A: I felt a tightness in my lower back right away, but I didn't think much of it. By the next morning it was a lot worse,
with stiffness and pain when I bent or sat for long periods.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to a clinic a couple of days later. They diagnosed a back strain and gave me instructions for physical
therapy and pain management.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add before we conclude?
A: No, I think that covers it.
Q: Thank you for your time. We will follow up with you in writing.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page

- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any

- "reason": one short sentence.
